overall_summary: Deduplication and recency-weighted analysis indicate that space and astronomy scenarios—specifically extreme exoplanet environments and hypothetical 'What If' space situations—significantly outperform general psychology, standard biology facts, or historical trivia. Videos featuring planetary hazards ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') and bizarre cosmic conditions generate superior view counts, likes-per-view, and engagement. Conversely, straightforward human psychology and general animal facts show low momentum and weak engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) heavily outperform standard factual statements.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersive survival scenarios inside bizarre planetary environments rather than static descriptive facts.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing extreme planetary properties like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) capture strong organic reach.
winning_patterns.action: Focus future space topics on counter-intuitive, physically jarring cosmic extremes that challenge basic human intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) consistently underperform in velocity and engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize human psychology and internal brain trivia in favor of grand-scale physical science and space.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' show suppressed momentum compared to high-concept space hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid basic trivia frameworks; if animal content is produced, shift it toward cinematic survival or prehistoric/deep-sea horror micro-narratives.
